statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(queries), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), writing l = queries[i][0] and m = queries[i][1], we have r[i] = arr[l] XOR arr[l+1] XOR ... XOR arr[m], i.e. r[i] is the bitwise XOR of all arr[j] with l <= j <= m. This range is non-empty because l <= m.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 1 and len(queries) >= 1; len(arr) <= 30000 and len(queries) <= 30000; for every k with 0 <= k < len(arr), 1 <= arr[k] <= 1000000000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(queries), len(queries[i]) = 2 and 0 <= queries[i][0] <= queries[i][1] < len(arr).
